title: One-page project status report
metaDescription: A one-page project status template that fits on a single screen: headline, status, key changes, risks, decisions needed, and next milestone. Husn fills it from your tools.
heroSubheadline: A status report should fit on one screen and still say something. This template holds the six things a reader needs, and Husn can fill it from the work so it stays current.
primaryPain: Most one-pagers are one page in name only, then a second page of caveats and a third of charts nobody opens, because no one was willing to decide what to leave out.
painBullets: The headline ends up below the fold, so a busy reader closes the page before they reach the line that mattered.
Risks and decisions get folded into a paragraph of progress, where they read as background instead of a prompt to act.
The single page is accurate the day it ships and wrong by the next meeting, because nobody updates a static document.
whyHardHeading: Why this gets hard at scale
whyHard: Fitting a real project onto one page forces choices about what to cut, and under deadline those choices fall to whoever is least informed.
A one-pager per project is fine. Forty of them, kept current by hand every week, is a job no one has time for.
The discipline that keeps a page short is the first thing to go when the news is bad, which is exactly when brevity helps the reader most.
howHusnHelps: Husn reads Jira, Slack, and docs and fills each section of the page, leading with the headline and the decisions, not the activity.
It keeps the page current as the work moves, so the version someone opens on Thursday reflects Thursday, not Monday.
Every line on the page links back to the issue, message, or document behind it, so a reader can check any claim without leaving the page.

useCases.body: Generate an accurate summary of a project you just inherited or stepped into, drawn from the work, not from a colleague's recollection.

useCases.title: Summaries at any altitude
useCases.body: Ask for a one-line version for a leader or a full page for a sponsor from the same read, so the facts hold across every level.

useCases.title: Pre-meeting prep
useCases.body: Generate a current summary before a meeting so the room starts from the same accurate picture instead of competing recollections.

faq.q: How is this different from pasting notes into a summarizer?
faq.a: A generic summarizer paraphrases the text you give it. Husn reads across your Jira, Slack, and docs first, so the summary covers what you would have missed, not just what you pasted.

faq.q: Can it write at different levels of detail?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for a sentence or a page from the same underlying read, and the altitude changes while the facts stay consistent.

faq.q: Can I verify what the summary says?
faq.a: Yes. Every line links back to the source it came from, so any claim in the summary can be checked in a click.

faq.q: Does it change anything in our tools?
faq.a: No. Husn reads and explains only. It never writes back to Jira, Slack, or your documents.

title: OKR status report
metaDescription: An OKR status report that connects objectives to the work actually moving them. Husn reads Jira, Slack, and docs and shows where progress and the OKRs have drifted apart.
heroHeadline: OKR status, grounded in the work.
heroSubheadline: OKRs are usually updated by self-rated confidence in a spreadsheet. Husn connects each key result to the work actually moving it, and shows where the score and the reality have drifted apart.
primaryPain: OKR check-ins typically run on a color and a number that an owner sets by feel, disconnected from the Jira and Slack where the work lives, so a key result can read on track for weeks while the work behind it has stalled.
painBullets: Confidence scores are self-reported, so optimism and politics shape the number as much as the actual progress does.
The OKR lives in one tool and the work lives in another, so nobody is watching whether the two still agree.
By the time a green key result is admitted to be red, the quarter is usually too far gone to recover it.
whyHardHeading: Why this gets hard at scale
whyHard: Tying an objective to the specific work moving it means reading across many tickets and threads, which a quarterly spreadsheet update never does.
Self-rated confidence drifts from reality slowly and invisibly, so the gap is widest exactly when no one is looking for it.
Across many teams and objectives, checking each score against the underlying work by hand is impossible, so the scores go unchallenged.
howHusnHelps: Husn reads across Jira, Slack, and docs and connects each key result to the work actually moving it, so the score has evidence behind it.
It surfaces where a confident OKR and the underlying work have drifted apart, while there is still a quarter left to act.
Every assessment links back to the issues and threads it draws from, so a leader can see why a key result is on or off track.

items.text: A key result rated green has had no underlying work move in three weeks, and the quarter is half gone.
The scope of an objective shifted in a planning thread but the key results were never updated to match.
Two objectives depend on the same team, whose capacity was cut after the targets were set.

useCases.title: Mid-quarter check-in
useCases.body: Review OKRs against the work that is actually moving them, so a drifting key result surfaces while the quarter can still be saved.

useCases.title: Leadership OKR review
useCases.body: Bring leadership scores grounded in evidence, not self-rated confidence, so the conversation is about reality instead of optimism.

useCases.title: Connecting strategy to delivery
useCases.body: Show which objectives have real work behind them and which are stalling, so attention and capacity move to where outcomes are at risk.

faq.q: How is this different from a confidence score?
faq.a: A confidence score is a feeling an owner records. Husn connects each key result to the work moving it, so the status rests on evidence, not optimism.

faq.q: Can it catch an OKR drifting off track?
faq.a: Yes. Husn surfaces when a key result rated green has no underlying work moving, so the drift shows up while there is still a quarter left to act.

faq.q: Where does it draw its evidence?
faq.a: From your Jira, Slack, and documents. Husn reads across them and ties the work it finds back to each objective and key result.

faq.q: Does Husn change anything in our tools?
faq.a: No. Husn reads and explains only. It never writes back to Jira, Slack, or your documents.
